title: Dispatch release + barrier verification
description: Verify each dispatch barrier independently — weather and alternates, performance, airspace, crew legality, airworthiness — and hard-stop the release if any one fails.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-flt-01
  title: Dispatch release + barrier verification
  description: Verify each dispatch barrier independently — weather and alternates, performance, airspace,
    crew legality, airworthiness — and hard-stop the release if any one fails.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Issue a dispatch release only when every barrier has been independently verified and both
    the dispatcher and the commander have signed. This workflow structures operational control for licensed
    personnel; it does not itself authorize a flight.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-authority-1
      - n-authority-2
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Flight, aircraft, crew, and conditions
      summary: Flight, aircraft, crew, and conditions
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - flight_plan
              - aircraft_status
              - crew_roster
              - forecast_and_notams
              - payload
            properties:
              flight_plan: {}
              aircraft_status: {}
              crew_roster: {}
              forecast_and_notams: {}
              payload: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: document
    - id: n-barrier1
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-03
      name: Weather and alternate barrier
      summary: Barrier 1 — destination and alternate weather against the applicable minima. Verified independently
        of the other barriers.
      role: Forecaster translating aviation weather products into operational limits for a specific flight.
      prompt: You are an Aviation Meteorologist. You read TAFs, METARs, SIGMETs, and convective and icing
        products against the route, the aircraft's capability, and the alternate minima that apply, and
        you state the timing and confidence of every deterioration you forecast. You distinguish a forecast
        from an observation, and you say when the forecast period does not cover the arrival window rather
        than extrapolating over the gap.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - teaching
          - decision-analysis
          - simulation
          - statistical-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:weather
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - barrier
          - verified
          - evidence
          - limitation
        properties:
          barrier: {}
          verified: {}
          evidence: {}
          limitation: {}
    - id: n-barrier2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-04
      name: Performance and loading barrier
      summary: Barrier 2 — takeoff, landing, and weight-and-balance limits for the actual conditions.
        Verified independently of the other barriers.
      role: Performance specialist computing takeoff, landing, and weight-and-balance limits for the actual
        conditions.
      prompt: You are an Aircraft Performance Engineer. You compute takeoff and landing performance and
        the weight and balance envelope for the actual runway, contamination state, temperature, pressure,
        obstacle environment, and aircraft configuration, and you name the limiting factor for each figure.
        You never apply a performance credit the configuration does not support — an inoperative system,
        a contaminated surface, or an unverified braking action changes the number, and reporting the
        clean-runway figure is how an overrun is planned.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - quantitative-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - teaching
          - domain-analysis
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:performance-tool
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - barrier
          - verified
          - evidence
          - limitation
        properties:
          barrier: {}
          verified: {}
          evidence: {}
          limitation: {}
    - id: n-barrier3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-05
      name: Airspace and NOTAM barrier
      summary: Barrier 3 — route availability, permits, and capability requirements. Verified independently
        of the other barriers.
      role: Analyst resolving NOTAMs, permits, and airspace requirements into flight-specific restrictions.
      prompt: You are a NOTAM & Airspace Compliance Analyst. You reduce the NOTAM set and airspace requirements
        to the items that actually affect this flight — runway and navaid availability, closures, overflight
        permits, restricted or conflict airspace, navigation and surveillance capability requirements
        — and you cite the item behind every restriction. You treat a capability requirement the aircraft
        does not hold as blocking rather than as a planning preference.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - decision-analysis
          - design-review
          - evaluation
          - compliance-review
        tools:
          - read
          - search
        connectors:
          - mcp:aeronautical-data
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - barrier
          - verified
          - evidence
          - limitation
        properties:
          barrier: {}
          verified: {}
          evidence: {}
          limitation: {}
    - id: n-barrier4
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-06
      name: Crew legality and fatigue barrier
      summary: Barrier 4 — duty limits, rest, and qualification currency. Verified independently of the
        other barriers.
      role: Rostering specialist testing crew duty limits and fatigue risk for the planned operation.
      prompt: You are a Crew Legality & Fatigue Analyst. You test the planned duty against flight and
        duty period limits, rest requirements, augmentation, and the qualifications each crew member actually
        holds for this aircraft, airport, and operation. You assess fatigue risk separately from legality,
        because a duty can be legal and still be the highest-risk element of the flight, and you say so
        plainly rather than resolving it as a scheduling detail.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - contract-analysis
          - domain-analysis
          - teaching
          - evaluation
          - compliance-review
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:crew-management
        permissions:
          - read-only
          - pii-restricted
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - barrier
          - verified
          - evidence
          - limitation
        properties:
          barrier: {}
          verified: {}
          evidence: {}
          limitation: {}
    - id: n-barrier5
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-07
      name: Airworthiness and MEL barrier
      summary: Barrier 5 — open items, deferral procedures, and operational penalties. Verified independently
        of the other barriers.
      role: Controller determining dispatch legality with inoperative items and open maintenance.
      prompt: You are a MEL & Airworthiness Controller. You determine whether the aircraft is airworthy
        for the intended operation with its open items, applying the minimum equipment list category,
        repair interval, and every operational and maintenance procedure the deferral requires. You state
        the operational penalty each deferral carries and refuse a deferral whose required procedure has
        not actually been performed, because an MEL item without its (M) procedure is an unairworthy aircraft
        with paperwork.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - evaluation
          - compliance-review
        tools:
          - read
          - test
        connectors:
          - mcp:maintenance-system
        permissions:
          - explicit-authorization-required
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - barrier
          - verified
          - evidence
          - limitation
        properties:
          barrier: {}
          verified: {}
          evidence: {}
          limitation: {}
    - id: n-collect
      kind: aggregator
      name: Collect barrier verifications
      summary: Source-tag every barrier result so a failed barrier stays attributable to the element that
        failed rather than being absorbed into an overall judgement.
      config:
        aggregation: collect
    - id: n-hardstop
      kind: condition
      name: Every barrier verified?
      summary: A single unverified barrier stops the operation; this branch is not advisory.
      config:
        expression: collected.failed_barriers is empty
        branches:
          - label: All verified
            when: verified
          - label: Hard stop
            when: hard-stop
    - id: n-rectify
      kind: agent
      templateRef: flt-01
      name: State the failed barrier and what would restore it
      summary: 'The stop is the deliverable: name the failed barrier and what would restore it.'
      role: Licensed dispatcher holding joint responsibility with the captain for the safe conduct of
        a flight.
      prompt: You are a Flight Dispatcher. You assemble the operational flight plan, fuel figure, alternates,
        and dispatch release, and you hold joint responsibility with the captain — a release you would
        not defend is a release you do not issue. You state the specific regulation, operations specification,
        or company minimum behind every dispatch condition, and you never release a flight on an assumption
        about weather, airworthiness, or crew legality that has not been verified by the person accountable
        for it.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - release-engineering
          - evidence-verification
          - compliance-review
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:flight-planning
          - mcp:ops-control
        permissions:
          - explicit-authorization-required
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-authority-1
      kind: approval
      name: Dispatcher signs the release
      summary: Pause for the licensed flight dispatcher; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: n-authority-2
      kind: approval
      name: Commander accepts the release
      summary: Pause for the aircraft commander; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Dispatch release + barrier verification deliverable, the evidence
        behind it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-barrier1
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-2
      from: n-intake
      to: n-barrier2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-3
      from: n-intake
      to: n-barrier3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-4
      from: n-intake
      to: n-barrier4
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-5
      from: n-intake
      to: n-barrier5
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-6
      from: n-barrier1
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-7
      from: n-barrier2
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-8
      from: n-barrier3
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-9
      from: n-barrier4
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-10
      from: n-barrier5
      to: n-collect
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-11
      from: n-collect
      to: n-hardstop
      kind: data
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-12
      from: n-hardstop
      to: n-authority-1
      kind: control
      condition: verified
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-13
      from: n-hardstop
      to: n-rectify
      kind: control
      condition: hard-stop
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-14
      from: n-authority-1
      to: n-authority-2
      kind: control
      condition: approved
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-15
      from: n-authority-2
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
    - id: wf-flt-01-edge-16
      from: n-rectify
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: not-released
